plain.li: Ate standing up again. We need a table.
Supper on an upturned crate. My back has opinions about it.
[winter] Ate my stew on the floor with my coat still on.
[child] We had supper on the floor, like a picnic.
Ate supper sitting on a sack of rice.
Lunch on the steps, with the bowl balanced on my knees.
Spilled half my soup down my front trying to eat off my lap.
Ate leaning against the wall. My bowl kept tipping.
[winter] Ate standing by the hearth to keep warm, since there was nowhere to sit anyway.
[child] I ate sitting on the floor next to the door.

warm.li: Sat on the floor with the others to eat. It was almost nice, all of us in a row against the wall.
No table, so we sat in a circle on the floor and passed the bread around.
Ate on the step with the others. We could do with a table, but the company was good.

blunt.li: No table. Again.
Build a table.
Eating off my knees. Enough.

cheerful.li: Floor picnic again! I'm getting good at balancing the bowl on my knees.
No table, so I ate lying on my stomach like at a picnic! Messy, but fun.
Floor supper again! I've found the one flat stone in the yard and claimed it.

gloomy.li: Ate off my knees like a dog. Maybe there'll be a table tomorrow.
No table, no chairs. We eat like people camped out waiting to leave.
Ate on the floor again. I don't know why it bothers me so much, but it does.

cold.li: Meal taken without a table. Bad for digestion and worse for morale.
No table. It's a few planks and an afternoon. I don't understand the delay.
Dining without a table. Civilized people don't eat this way.

plain.li: Raw rice for lunch. I chewed and chewed and it never got any softer.
Nothing cooked today, so I ate a potato raw, skin and all.
[winter] Ate a raw ear of corn so cold it hurt my teeth.
[child] I ate a raw potato because supper was taking too long. It tasted like dirt.
Chewed on a raw turnip for supper. My jaw aches.
Ate a raw egg because nothing else was ready. I'd rather not do that again.
[winter] Gnawed on frozen berries for lunch. They hurt my teeth.

warm.li: The cook is sick, so it was raw potatoes tonight. I took the cook some water on my way to bed.
The cooks were busy, so I shared my raw carrots around.
Ate raw today so the cook could rest. I don't mind, once in a while.

blunt.li: Ate it raw. Somebody learn to cook.
Raw again. Somebody cook.
Raw rice. Never again.

cheerful.li: Raw corn for lunch! It's sweeter than you'd think, if you don't mind the crunch.
Raw carrots for lunch! Crunchy, at least.
I ate a raw potato and told myself it was an apple.

gloomy.li: Chewed raw rice straight from the sack. My stomach's been complaining since noon.
Raw food again. My stomach's been complaining since noon.
Ate it raw because I was too tired to wait. My belly's paying for it.

cold.li: Took the meat raw. It saves fuel, and the cramps pass.
Raw food. Whoever is meant to be cooking is not.
Ate it uncooked. Unpleasant, but it fills the stomach.

plain.li: Proper supper tonight, meat and potatoes with real gravy.
Whoever cooked today knew what they were doing. I wiped the bowl clean with my finger.
A good hot meal, and nothing urgent after it. I sat a while with the empty bowl.
[child] Supper was really good today. I ate all of it, even the green bits.
Stew with real meat in it tonight, and bread to wipe the bowl.
Good supper. The cook put something in the potatoes I couldn't name, and I had seconds.
Ate a proper meal sitting down, with no one calling for me halfway through.
Hot food, a full bowl and a seat at the table. I can't ask for more on a workday.
Meat pie for lunch. The crust was dark on one side and I ate every crumb anyway.
[child] I ate my whole supper and then helped scrape the pot.

warm.li: Good meal tonight. I made a point of telling the cook.
The cook saved me a bowl when I came in late. It was still hot.
Shared a good supper with the others, and for once we didn't talk about work.
Took a plate up to whoever was on watch, so they'd eat while it was hot.

blunt.li: Decent food. More of that.
Good food. Cook knows the job.
Full belly. Back to work.

cheerful.li: There were herbs in the stew tonight! I'm still thinking about it.
The stew had real carrots in it tonight. Big ones!
Second helpings tonight! I took mine before the cook could change their mind.

gloomy.li: A good meal for once. I ate slowly so it would last.
Good meal tonight. We'll be back to scraps by the end of the week, I expect.
Ate well tonight. I can't stop thinking about the days when we didn't.

cold.li: Fine meal. The cook is worth keeping.
A proper meal. Well-fed people make fewer mistakes, and I made none today.
Ate well. I noticed who took the biggest portions.

plain.li: Lavish meal tonight. Roast, buttered corn, and something sweet after.
Ate so much I had to lie down afterward.
[trait:Gourmand] Two helpings of the roast, and I'd have had a third if there'd been one.
[child] We had a feast for supper! I ate until my belly was round.
The table was covered tonight. I tried a bit of everything and then a bit more.
A proper feast of a supper. I'm still full writing this.
[child] There was pudding at supper. I had some, then I had some of someone else's.

warm.li: The cook spent all afternoon on supper. We stayed at the table long after the plates were empty.
The cook outdid themselves tonight. I took a plate up to whoever was on watch.
We lingered over the lavish supper, passing dishes and talking, and none of us in a hurry.

blunt.li: Best meal I've had here. Do it again.
Best supper in weeks. More nights like this.
Ate too much. Worth it.

cheerful.li: A lavish meal tonight! I licked the plate clean.
A feast! I had three kinds of everything.
There was dessert tonight. Actual dessert!

gloomy.li: Ate like a lord tonight. Tomorrow it's back to the usual.
A lavish supper. I ate it slowly, because tomorrow it's stew again.
Best meal in weeks. I don't know when the next one will be.

cold.li: Lavish meal. Expensive to make, and worth it for what it does to morale.
A lavish meal. Good for morale, and I'd ration them to keep it that way.
Feast tonight. People will work harder tomorrow, which is the point.

plain.li: Paste from the dispenser again. Gray, warm, and no taste at all.
Ate my paste standing next to the dispenser. It's quicker that way.
Nutrient paste. I've stopped guessing what went into the hopper.
[child] We had paste for lunch. I drew a face in mine with my spoon.
Paste for breakfast and paste for supper. At least I know what's coming.
Someone stirred a pinch of salt into the paste today. It nearly tasted like food.
[child] The paste looks like porridge if you squint.

warm.li: It's only paste, but it's warm, and there's always enough to go around.
Ate my paste with the others, and we made a game of guessing what it was meant to taste like.
Paste again, but it's hot and filling, and the cooks have better things to do than fuss over me.

blunt.li: Paste. I want real food.
Paste. Again.
I'd trade a day's work for real bread.

cheerful.li: If you eat it fast enough, you barely taste the paste!
Paste! I've decided it tastes like soup today.
I've started giving the paste flavors in my head. Today was roast fowl!

gloomy.li: Fifth day of paste in a row. I can't remember what salt tastes like.
Paste. I don't even taste it anymore.
Gray food in a gray bowl. That was supper.

cold.li: Efficient stuff, paste. It frees the cooks for other work.
Paste is adequate nutrition. Morale is someone else's department.
I eat the paste quickly and get back to work. It saves time.

plain.li: Stomach growling all afternoon. Supper can't come soon enough.
Skipped lunch to finish the north wall. I've regretted it every hour since.
[winter] Rations are thin this winter. I've moved my belt in another notch.
[child] I'm hungry. I asked twice when supper was and they said soon.
[trait:Gourmand] Had a full meal at noon and was hungry again before I'd washed the bowl.
Missed lunch hauling stone. I could smell the kitchen all afternoon.
Drank a cup of water to fill my stomach. It didn't last.
Ate a handful of berries off a bush on the way back. Not nearly enough.
My stomach growled during the meeting, and the person next to me heard it.
[winter] Short rations again. I finished my bowl and looked around for more.
[winter] The stores are low and we all know it. I eat slowly to make it last.
[child] My tummy hurts from being hungry.
[trait:Gourmand] Only two meals today. I spent the afternoon planning the third.

warm.li: I'm hungry, but so are the others. We'll eat well when the harvest comes in.
Gave my bread to someone who needed it more. I'll eat well tomorrow.
Hungry, but there's stew on for tomorrow. I can smell it from here.

blunt.li: Hungry. Where's the food?
Starving. Cook something.
Feed us properly.

cheerful.li: So hungry I could eat a whole muffalo! I'd settle for a potato.
So hungry I'd eat the cook's apron! Supper had better be big.
Hungry today, so tomorrow's breakfast will taste twice as good!

gloomy.li: Went to bed hungry, thinking about bread.
Another day on half rations. My belt's on its last hole.
Hungry again. It's starting to feel normal, and that frightens me.

cold.li: An empty stomach slows my work. Someone should account for that.
I'm hungry, which means someone planned the food badly.
Underfed today. I'll be slower tomorrow, and so will everyone else on half rations.

plain.li: Couldn't get warm last night. I lay there listening to the wind until it got light.
Slept in my coat and boots and still woke up shivering.
[winter] There was frost on my blanket when I woke up.
[child] It was so cold last night I could see my breath in bed.
Woke at dawn curled in a ball with my knees up to my chin.
Spent half the night getting up to pile more on the bed. None of it helped.
The wind found every gap in the wall last night.
Couldn't feel my toes when I got up. I stamped around the room until they came back.
[winter] Woke up and the water in my cup had a skin of ice on it.
[winter] Slept in everything I own, and the cold still got into my back.
[winter] Three blankets and my coat over the top, and I was still shivering at dawn.
[child] I warmed my feet on the hearthstones before bed, but they went cold again under the blanket.

warm.li: Cold night. There was an extra blanket on my bed when I came in, and I don't know who put it there.
Cold night. I gave my spare blanket to the youngest and slept in my coat.
We pushed the beds together for warmth last night, elbows and all.

blunt.li: Froze all night. My feet still haven't warmed up.
Cold room. Fix the walls.
Didn't sleep. Too cold.

cheerful.li: Curled up tight like a squirrel and made it through the cold night!
Frost on the inside of the window this morning. I drew a face in it!
Cold night, but hot tea in the morning made up for it!

gloomy.li: Cold again. I've stopped expecting to be warm before spring.
Cold seeps up through the floor at night. I can't remember the last time my feet were warm.
Another freezing night. I lay awake wishing the morning would hurry up.

cold.li: Slept badly in the cold. The room needs a fire in it, or I need a different room.
Slept cold. I'll be slow tomorrow, and I'll say exactly why if anyone asks.
The bedroom drops below freezing after midnight. I left a cup of water out to be sure.

plain.li: Too hot to sleep. I lay on top of the blanket and sweated through it anyway.
Woke up three times in the night, soaked. The air in that room doesn't move.
[summer] Another sticky night. I slept with my feet pressed against the cool wall.
[child] It was too hot to sleep, so I counted the cracks in the ceiling.
Lay awake in the heat listening to the insects. Got up twice to splash water on my face.
Slept on the floor because the bed was too warm. The floor wasn't much better.
Woke up with my shirt stuck to my back.
The room was like an oven last night. I dragged my mattress over to the doorway.
[summer] Hot night again. Not a breath of wind through the window.
[summer] I've started sleeping with a wet cloth on my chest. It's dry by midnight.
[summer] Another night too hot for blankets, or clothes, or sleep.
[child] It was too hot, so I slept on the floor with my cheek on the cool stones.

warm.li: Hot night. A few of us gave up on sleep and sat in the doorway talking until it cooled off.
Hot night. I fetched cold water for everyone in our room before I lay down.
Too hot to sleep, so I sat outside with whoever else was awake. Good company, at least.

blunt.li: Too hot. Didn't sleep.
Hot room. No sleep. Fix it.
Sweated all night. I'm done with that room.

cheerful.li: Hot night, so I slept with a wet cloth over my face! It mostly worked.
Too hot to sleep, so I counted the stars from the doorway! I got to two hundred.
Slept on top of the covers with my feet in a bucket of water. Best idea I've had all week!

gloomy.li: Another night sweating into the mattress. I'm too tired to complain properly.
Hot again. I lay there sticky and awake, thinking about all the things I can't fix.
The heat never lets up. I'm starting to forget what a cool night feels like.

cold.li: Slept poorly in the heat. A cooler in that room would pay for itself in a week.
Heat ruined my sleep. That room was built with no thought for air.
I slept two hours in the heat. My work tomorrow will show it.

plain.li: Woke up on the ground with a root in my back.
Rolled up in my coat on the bare floor last night. My shoulder's stiff.
[rain] It rained on me in the night. Everything I own is damp.
[child] I slept outside under the stars. A beetle walked across my face.
Slept curled up by the wall with my coat over my head.
Woke up with dew on my blanket and an ant in my ear.
[rain] Woke up in a puddle. I didn't know I could sleep through that.

warm.li: We all bedded down on the floor together. Somebody snored, and I found it comforting.
Slept under the stars with the others. Someone pointed out the shapes the old people used to see in them.
No beds yet, so we slept back to back to keep warm.

blunt.li: Slept in the dirt. I want a bed.
Ground again. I want a bed.
Slept in the dirt. My back hates me.

cheerful.li: Under the stars last night! I saw a shooting star and made a wish.
Slept outside and watched the stars until I dropped off! I didn't even mind the rocks.
Camped out last night! It felt like an adventure.

gloomy.li: Another night on the ground like an animal. My hip still aches from it.
Another night on the bare ground. I feel like a stray dog.
Cold earth and a stone for a pillow. I'm too old for this.

cold.li: Slept on the ground. A bed costs some wood and an afternoon, and I'd like to know why I don't have one.
No bed. The ground is cold and the sleep is poor. Someone should fix it.
Slept rough. I can't work well after nights like this.

plain.li: Someone kept walking past my bed all night, in heavy boots.
Woke up every time the door opened. Whoever's hauling at night, please stop.
Barely slept. Footsteps, then the door, then footsteps again.
[child] Grown-ups kept walking past my bed in the night. I couldn't get back to sleep.
Somebody dropped a pot in the night. I lay awake for ages after.
Woke to someone coughing, then someone snoring, then a door.
Couldn't sleep for the comings and goings. Every time I drifted off, someone else came in.
The door creaks. I know because I heard it eleven times last night.
[child] Somebody woke me up in the night by mistake. I was having a good dream.

warm.li: Somebody tripped over the end of my bed in the dark. We both laughed and went back to sleep.
Someone was up with a sick stomach all night. I got up and sat with them for a while.
Woken twice in the night. Once it was someone bringing me a blanket, and I didn't mind that.

blunt.li: Stop stomping past my bed at night.
Quiet at night. Is that so hard?
Woken again. I'm moving my bed.

cheerful.li: Woke up a few times when people went by. Had good dreams in between!
Woken three times in the night, so I had three dreams instead of one!
Somebody tripped over my boots in the dark and said a word I'd never heard before!

gloomy.li: Every time I got to sleep, someone came through. I've given up on a full night.
Broken sleep again. I feel like I've been awake for days.
Lay awake listening to footsteps. Even when they stopped, I kept waiting for more.

cold.li: Sleep interrupted by foot traffic. My bed needs moving out of the path.
Woken four times. I've worked out who it was each time.
Disturbed sleep. Whoever keeps hauling at night should be put on the day shift.

plain.li: Barracks again. One snorer at the far end, and one who grinds their teeth.
Got dressed under the blanket. There's nowhere else to do it in the barracks.
I'd give a lot for a door I could close.
[child] I sleep in the big room with the grown-ups. They snore louder than me.
Someone talks in their sleep in the barracks. Last night it was about turnips.
Six people breathing in one room. You'd think I'd be used to it by now.
Woke up with someone's foot hanging off the next bed onto mine.
I keep my things in a sack under my pillow. It's the only part of the barracks that's mine.
[child] Someone in the big room snores like a bear. I counted the snores until I fell asleep.

warm.li: The barracks are crowded, but there's always someone awake if you can't sleep.
I like hearing the others breathe in the barracks. It means we all made it home.
Showed the new one where the spare blankets are kept in the barracks tonight.

blunt.li: I want my own room.
Barracks. Snoring. No sleep.
Give me a door. That's all.

cheerful.li: We whispered jokes across the beds in the barracks until someone threw a boot!
Someone told a ghost story in the barracks after dark, and we all laughed instead of screaming!
Woke up in the barracks to somebody's terrible singing, so I joined in!

gloomy.li: Another night in the barracks. I can't remember the last time I was alone.
Still in the barracks. I've given up asking when that'll change.
Never alone, not even at night. It wears on you.

cold.li: Slept in the barracks. I'd sleep better with a lock between me and the others.
Barracks again. I keep my valuables on me.
Communal sleeping is efficient for the colony. Not for me.

plain.li: [good] Slept well in my own room, with the door shut and the rug warm under my feet.
[good] Woke up and lay in bed a while, looking at the painting on my wall.
[bad] The draft under my door woke me twice. The floor's still dirt.
[bad] Woke up and stared at the stains on the wall. I need to do something about that room.
[good,child] I love my room. I have my own blanket and my own shelf.
[bad,child] I don't like my room. It's ugly and it smells bad.
[good] Aired my blanket in the sun this morning. Slept in it tonight and it still smelled of outside.
[good] Hung my coat on the peg, shut the door, and had the whole room to myself.
[good] My room is quiet at night. I can hear the wind and not much else.
[good] Moved my bed away from the window so the morning light lands on my feet instead of my face.
[bad] Damp smell in my room again. I checked under the bed and behind the dresser and couldn't find where it's coming from.
[bad] Lay in bed counting the cracks in my wall. There are more than last month.
[bad] To reach my door I have to climb over the end of the bed.
[bad] Bare walls, bare floor, one blanket. I sleep there, and that's all I can say for it.
[good,child] I put my best stones on the shelf in my room, in a row from biggest to smallest.
[bad,child] My room is dark, and at night the coat on the hook looks like a man standing there.

warm.li: [good] I've made my room nice, bit by bit. Tonight it felt like home.
[bad] Swept my room out tonight. It isn't much, but I'll make it better.
[good] Woke early and lay listening to the others moving about outside my door. I like knowing they're there.
[good] Someone left a bunch of dried flowers on my windowsill. My room smells of them now.
[bad] The room's cold and plain. I tacked a blanket over the worst gap in the wall and called it a start.
[bad] My room isn't much, but I made the bed properly and put my things in order before I slept.

blunt.li: [good] Good room. Good sleep.
[bad] Room's a hole. Fix it or give me another.
[good] Slept. Door shut. No complaints.
[good] Best sleep in weeks. Leave the room as it is.
[bad] Dirt floor, no rug, damp walls. Somebody fix it.
[bad] My room's an ugly box.

cheerful.li: [good] Slept like a baby in my lovely room! I didn't want to get up.
[bad] My room is a disgrace, but I've decided it's cozy!
[good] Woke up in my own bed in my own room and stretched until my toes cracked!
[good] I've arranged my room exactly how I like it. Tonight I just sat on the bed and looked at it.
[bad] My room is ugly, but the biggest stain on the wall looks like a duck, and now I'm fond of it.
[bad] Cramped room. If I lie corner to corner, I fit!

gloomy.li: [good] A fine room and a good night's sleep. I keep waiting for someone to take it away.
[bad] Filthy, cramped room. I'm too tired to do anything about it.
[good] Nice room, soft bed. I still woke at every sound.
[good] I slept, for once. It must be the room.
[bad] Lay on my bed and watched the damp patch spread across the ceiling.
[bad] My room is the sort of place you'd lock a prisoner in.

cold.li: [good] The room suits my position. People notice where you sleep.
[bad] My room is an insult. I've noted who has the better ones.
[good] Slept well. A good room pays for itself in the work I do the next day.
[good] The room is adequate. I intend to keep it, and to keep other people out of it.
[bad] A room this bad tells me exactly what the council thinks of me.
[bad] Poor sleep in a poor room. I'll be slower tomorrow, and that's on whoever decides the rooms.

plain.li: Dead on my feet. Nearly nodded off standing at the workbench.
Too tired to write much.
Yawned all afternoon. My eyes keep closing as I write this.
[child] I fell asleep at lunch with my spoon in my hand.
Fell asleep sitting on a crate and woke up with a crick in my neck.
Did the same job twice today because I forgot I'd done it the first time.
My eyes are gritty and my hands are slow. Bed, now.
Dropped a whole tray today. Too tired to hold things properly.
[child] I yawned so big my jaw clicked.

warm.li: Exhausted. The others finished my hauling while I sat down for a minute.
Fell asleep at supper, and someone put a blanket over me instead of waking me.
Dead tired, but the others are too. We'll all sleep well tonight.

blunt.li: Need sleep. Now.
Exhausted. Going to bed.
No more work today. I'm done.

cheerful.li: So tired I laughed at a bucket for no reason!
So sleepy I tried to put my boot on my hand! Bed now.
Tired, but the good kind. I'll sleep like a stone tonight!

gloomy.li: Tired in my bones. Sleep doesn't fix it anymore.
Woke up tired, worked tired, going to bed tired.
I don't remember the last time I woke up rested.

cold.li: Exhausted. My work is getting sloppy, which costs more than the sleep would.
Too little sleep. I made two mistakes today that I wouldn't have made rested.
Exhausted. I'm taking the late shift off, allowed or not.

plain.li: Ate in the dining room. Clean table, good chairs, and the statue in the corner watching us chew.
Supper at the long table tonight. The room is starting to look like somewhere people live.
Took my time over supper. It's a good room to sit in.
[child] We ate in the big room with the pretty rug. I didn't spill anything.
Supper at the long table, with candles down the middle and no one in a hurry.
The dining room was full tonight. It's the best room we have.
Sat with my back to the warm wall and ate slowly.
Stayed at the table after the plates were cleared. Good chairs make you linger.
[child] I sat on the big chair at supper and my feet didn't touch the floor.

warm.li: Supper in the dining room with the others. I like that room best at night, when it's full.
Supper in the dining room. Someone raised a cup to the cook, and we all joined in.
I sat next to someone I don't usually talk to tonight. Good conversation, good room.

blunt.li: Nice dining room. Food tastes better in it.
Good room. Good meal.
Ate in the dining room. Better than the floor.

cheerful.li: Ate at the good table tonight! I felt like a guest at a lord's house.
Ate in the fancy dining room! I used my best manners and everything.
Lovely supper in the dining room, and we stayed until the candles burned down!

gloomy.li: The dining room is lovely. I still ate the same old stew in it.
The dining room's very fine. I sat in it and thought about who isn't here to see it.
Supper in the good room. In there it's easy to forget what's outside.

cold.li: Dined in the good room. People work harder after eating somewhere decent.
The dining room impresses visitors. It impressed me, which I didn't expect.
Ate in the good room. It was worth what it cost.

plain.li: Played horseshoes after work. Lost every game, but it's a nice room to lose in.
Read in the games room until my eyes hurt. Good chairs in there.
[!lowtech] Sat in the rec room with the others and watched the television.
[child] I played in the games room until bedtime. I almost won at chess.
Played cards in the games room after supper and won a few hands.
Sat by the window in the rec room and did nothing all evening. It was wonderful.
Lost three games of horseshoes in a row. Still a good evening.
The games room was full tonight, and loud.
[!lowtech] Played billiards in the rec room. I'm getting better at the bank shots.
[child] I played hide-and-seek in the games room, and they didn't find me for ages.

warm.li: Good evening in the common room. Someone was humming, and the rest of us were too comfortable to move.
Games room tonight. Someone taught me a new game, and I taught them one back.
A good evening with the others in the common room. I laughed more than I have in a while.

blunt.li: Good room for a rest. Needed that.
Played games. Won some. Good night.
Rec room's good. Use it more.

cheerful.li: Won two games of chess tonight!
Won at horseshoes, then lost at everything else. Still counts!
Best evening in ages in the games room!

gloomy.li: Sat in the games room until late. It took my mind off things for an evening.
Games room tonight. For a few hours I didn't think about anything at all.
I went to the games room to forget about things. It worked until bedtime.

cold.li: Spent the evening in the games room. Good for my mood, so good for my work.
An evening in the rec room. I watched how the others play. It says a lot about them.
Recreation done. I'll be sharper tomorrow for it.

plain.li: Worked most of the day in the dark. I can't tell if the floor is clean or not.
Stubbed my toe twice in the storeroom. There's no light back there at all.
[!lowtech] The lamp in the workshop is out again. I worked by feel.
[lowtech] The torches in the back room burned out before noon. I worked by feel after that.
[child] It's dark in the back rooms. I ran through them as fast as I could.
Couldn't find my own tools in the dark. Found someone else's instead.
Felt my way along the wall to the storeroom and put my hand in something wet.
Worked in the gloom all afternoon. My eyes ache from squinting.
Tripped over a bucket I couldn't see.
[!lowtech] Another lamp burned out in the hall. We're down to one at the far end.
[lowtech] We ran out of tallow for the candles. I worked by the light from the door.
[child] I'm scared of the dark storeroom. I made someone come with me.

warm.li: Dark in the workshop all day. The others kept talking so I'd know where they were.
Dark in the storeroom again. I held the door open so the others could see what they were doing.
Too dark to work well. I left a candle by the door for whoever comes next.

blunt.li: Too dark to work. Get us some light.
Dark again. Where's the light?
Can't work blind.

cheerful.li: Spent the day in the dark like a mole! I know the storeroom by touch now.
Dark in the back again. I found my way by humming and listening for the echo!
Pitch black in the storeroom! I found three things I'd lost by tripping over them.

gloomy.li: Dark all day. It gets into you after a while.
Gloomy rooms, gloomy work. It's hard to keep your spirits up in the dark.
Haven't seen proper light all day.

cold.li: Worked in poor light all day. I've started keeping a list of what it's cost us.
Poor lighting. Someone will get hurt in that storeroom.
Dark workrooms mean slow work and bad work. We have both.

plain.li: [good] The flowers by the path are out. I took the long way to the fields to walk past them.
[good] There's a new painting in the hall. I stopped to look at it every time I passed.
[bad] Old bloodstains on the floor, and the rubble still piled by the door.
[bad] Scrubbed one corner of the hall today. It made the rest look worse.
[good,child] There's a pretty statue in the hall. I said good morning to it.
[bad,child] Our house is ugly. I want to draw flowers on all the walls.
[good] Someone swept the yard and set a pot of flowers by the door. I noticed it on the way in.
[good] Walked the long way around the garden after supper, just to see it.
[good] The hall's been scrubbed and there's a new rug down. It looks like a home now.
[bad] Ash and bones from last week's cookfire are still lying in the yard where they fell.
[bad] Somebody was sick on the hall floor and it dried there. I stepped around it four times today.
[bad] Everything I looked at today was broken, dirty or half built.
[bad] There's been a smear on the storeroom wall for a week. I've started to think of it as part of the wall.
[good,child] Someone painted a picture in the hall. It has a horse in it.
[bad,child] There's mud everywhere. I made a mud pie on the floor and it fit right in.

warm.li: [good] Somebody planted roses by the door. The place is starting to look lovely.
[bad] It's been ugly here lately. I swept the hall after supper so we'd have one clean room.
[good] The garden by the kitchen is coming along. Whoever's been watering it, thank you.
[good] Stopped by the sculpture in the hall today and found two others already there, looking at it.
[bad] The place is a mess, but I've seen people picking things up as they pass. It'll come around.
[bad] Wiped the blood off the doorframe before the children could see it.

blunt.li: [good] Place looks good. Keep it that way.
[bad] This place is a pigsty. Clean it.
[good] Clean floors, flowers out front. More of this.
[good] Somebody did good work on the hall. It shows.
[bad] Rubble in the yard for a week. Haul it.
[bad] Filth everywhere. I'm done stepping in it.

cheerful.li: [good] Everything looks so pretty today! I stopped to smell every flower on the way to work.
[bad] It's ugly around here, so I've started carving a bird for the hall!
[good] There's a statue in the hall now, and I've decided it's smiling at me!
[good] Flowers by the path, a clean floor and sunshine. What a day.
[bad] Messy around here lately. I picked up three things on my way to supper, and I'll do three more tomorrow.
[bad] It's grim around here, so I've started whistling everywhere I go. It helps me, anyway.

gloomy.li: [good] Pretty around here lately. I give it until the next raid.
[bad] Dirt on the floors and blood on the walls. It wears on you.
[good] The flowers are nice. They won't last, but they're nice.
[good] Someone hung a painting and put down a rug in the hall. For a moment I forgot what's outside the walls.
[bad] Blood on the floor, rot in the corner and a wall that never got finished. That's the view from my seat at supper.
[bad] Ugly, dirty and gray. The place matches my mood.

cold.li: [good] Better surroundings lately, and my work has improved with them.
[bad] Ugly surroundings. I'd put two people on cleaning tomorrow.
[good] The colony looks prosperous lately. Visitors will notice, and so will raiders.
[good] Pleasant surroundings. People argue less in a clean hall.
[bad] Filth in the hall again. I counted four people who walked past it today, myself included.
[bad] The place looks abandoned. That isn't the impression we should be giving traders.

plain.li: Haven't seen the sky in days. I keep finding reasons to walk past the door.
Indoors all day again. I keep hearing birds outside.
[winter] Too cold to go out. The walls feel closer every day.
[child] I want to go outside and play. They keep saying not today.
Spent the whole day inside. I stood in the doorway at dusk just to breathe.
I've memorized every crack in these walls.
[winter] Snowed in again. I paced the hall until someone asked me to stop.

warm.li: Stuck inside all week. The others are good company, but I miss the wind.
Stuck inside with the others. We told stories to pass the time, but I'd give a lot for a walk.
Indoors again. I opened the shutters to let the light in for all of us.

blunt.li: Let me out of here.
Need to get outside. Today.
Four walls, no sky. Enough.

cheerful.li: Tomorrow I'm going outside, even if it's only to haul rocks!
Tomorrow I'm going for a long walk, whatever the weather!
I've been inside so long I waved at a bird through the window!

gloomy.li: Same walls, same ceiling, every day. I've forgotten what rain feels like.
The walls are closing in. I haven't felt the wind in days.
Indoors again. The days all feel the same in here.

cold.li: Confined too long. I'm short with people and I know why.
Too long indoors. I'm getting irritable, and others have noticed.
I need time outdoors. I'll take it, whatever's on the work list.

plain.li: Work, eat, sleep, work. I can't remember the last time I did anything for fun.
Whittled a stick down to a toothpick and threw it away.
Read the same book again. I could recite the third chapter.
[child] There's nothing to do. I asked three grown-ups to play and they all said later.
Counted the stones in the wall by my bed. There are forty-one.
Sat on the step after supper with nothing to do. Went to bed early.
Same work, same food, same faces. I need a day off.
Spent the evening carving a spoon I don't need.
Asked around for a game of anything. The others were all busy.
[child] I made up a game with two sticks and a stone. It wasn't very fun.

warm.li: So bored. Tomorrow I'll ask the others if anyone wants to play cards after supper.
Bored, so I offered to teach a card game to anyone who wanted to learn. Two said yes.
Nothing to do tonight. I sat with the others and listened to them talk.

blunt.li: Bored. Give me something to do that isn't work.
Bored stiff.
Nothing to do here but work. I need a break.

cheerful.li: Nothing to do, so I tried juggling potatoes! I'm not good at it yet.
Nothing to do, so I made a boat out of bark and sailed it in the water barrel!
Bored today. Tomorrow I'm organizing a game after supper, whether people like it or not!

gloomy.li: Every day is the same. I've stopped keeping track of which one it is.
Nothing to look forward to tomorrow, or the day after that.
I can't remember the last thing I did for fun.

cold.li: No recreation in days. My mood is slipping, and my work will follow it.
No recreation. People get careless when they're bored, and I'm no exception.
Spent the evening doing nothing. A waste, but there wasn't anything else.

plain.li: Soaked to the skin. My boots squelched all the way back from the field.
Got caught in the rain hauling wood. Everything I'm wearing is still damp.
[winter] Wet and cold at the same time. My fingers wouldn't bend when I got in.
[child] I got soaking wet. I jumped in every puddle on the way back.
Rain came down sideways today. I've wrung out my socks twice.
Slipped on the bank and went into the stream up to my waist.
Wet all day. My hands are white and wrinkled.
Hung my clothes near the stove to dry. They're still steaming.
[winter] Wet snow soaked me through by noon. I couldn't stop shaking until supper.
[child] My boots filled up with water and squelched all the way home.

warm.li: Came in dripping. The cook gave me something hot to hold while my clothes dried.
Came in soaked, and someone had already hung a towel by the door for me.
Got wet through, but I got the washing in before the worst of it.

blunt.li: Soaked. I hate rain.
Soaked. Need dry clothes.
Rain. All day. In it.

cheerful.li: Got drenched! I stayed out in it a while longer, since I was already wet.
Soaked to the bone! I danced in the rain, since I couldn't get any wetter.
Wet as a fish today, but the rain smelled wonderful.

gloomy.li: My clothes haven't been dry in three days.
Wet and cold and miserable. My boots will never dry.
Rain again, wet again. It's the third day running.

cold.li: Wet through at work. Cold hands are slow hands, and I lost most of the afternoon.
Working wet lowers output. We need covered walkways.
Soaked through. I hope someone is tracking how much work the weather costs us.

plain.li: My leg's been throbbing since morning. Hard to think about anything else.
Couldn't get comfortable all day. Every step pulls at the stitches.
Wrote this lying down. Sitting up hurts too much.
[child] My arm hurts. The doctor said it'll get better, but it still hurts now.
Every time I bend down, it catches me. I've stopped bending down.
Bit down on a strip of leather when they changed the dressing.
The ache comes in waves. Between them, I can almost work.
Slept badly. The pain doesn't care what time it is.

warm.li: In pain today. The others kept bringing me water without being asked.
The pain's bad today. Someone sat with me after supper and talked until I forgot about it.
It hurts, but I'm alive and the others are looking after me.

blunt.li: It hurts. Don't ask.
Pain. Leave me be.
Hurts like fire. Still standing.

cheerful.li: Hurts a lot today, but less than yesterday, so I'm counting that!
Ow, all day! But I can wiggle my toes again.
It hurts, but a bit less every day, and I'm keeping count!

gloomy.li: The pain is worse at night. I lie there and feel my heartbeat in it.
The pain won't let up. I'm forgetting what it was like before.
Hurt all day. I'm starting to think it won't ever heal right.

cold.li: Constant pain. I can still work. I'll say so if that changes.
In pain. I'll need longer to heal than the doctor said.
The pain affects my concentration. I've moved myself to simple work until it passes.

plain.li: My pants split at the knee today. I've run out of places to patch.
Patched my coat with a scrap of sack. It looks it.
[winter] The wind goes straight through the holes in my shirt.
[child] I tore my shirt climbing. Now you can see my belly.
My sleeve came off at the shoulder while I was hauling. I tied it back on with string.
The sole of my boot is flapping. I can hear it with every step.
Found a new hole in my coat this morning. I don't know where it came from.
Mended my shirt again. There's more thread in it than shirt now.
[winter] My mittens have holes in every finger.
[child] My knees are poking out of my pants.

warm.li: Clothes in tatters. I'll ask the tailor nicely when there's time.
Torn clothes, but I'll wait my turn. The tailor has enough on.
Patched a hole in someone else's shirt along with mine. Might as well, while the needle's out.

blunt.li: These clothes are rags. I need new ones.
Rags. New clothes, please.
My boots are done. So am I.

cheerful.li: My pants are more patch than pants now!
My pants have so many patches they're practically a quilt!
Ripped my shirt again! I'm calling it a window.

gloomy.li: Rags. I look like what's left behind after a raid.
Everything I own is wearing out, me included.
Threadbare clothes and a cold wind. I'm tired of being cold.

cold.li: People judge you by your clothes, whatever they say. Mine are falling apart.
Ragged clothes mark you as someone who doesn't matter. I won't wear these much longer.
Damaged clothing. I've asked the tailor twice now.

plain.li: Pulled on a dead man's pants this morning. They fit better than I'd like.
There's a neat hole in the back of this coat. I try not to think about how it got there.
Washed the shirt twice. It still feels like someone else's.
[child] My new shirt belonged to someone who died. It's too big and it smells funny.
Put on a jacket off a dead raider. There was still a heel of bread in the pocket.
Wearing boots taken off a body. They're the best I've had.

warm.li: This coat belonged to someone who didn't make it. I'll take good care of it.
These clothes belonged to someone. I said a word for them before I put them on.

blunt.li: Wearing a dead raider's coat. Better than freezing.
Dead man's shirt. Still a shirt.

cheerful.li: These boots came off a raider, but they're the best boots I've ever had!
A raider's hat, and it suits me!

gloomy.li: Dead man's shirt. One day someone will be wearing mine.
I'm wearing a dead man's coat. It still smells of its owner.

cold.li: The previous owner has no use for it. Good stitching.
The clothes fit. Their owner has no complaints.

plain.li: No clothes today. I kept to the back rooms as much as I could.
Spent the day without a stitch on. The wind found places I'd forgotten about.
[winter] It's winter and I have nothing to wear. I kept moving so I wouldn't freeze.
[child] My clothes got ruined and now I don't have any. I hid behind the crates.
No clothes. I've been wrapped in a blanket all day, which makes work hard.

warm.li: Nothing to wear yet. The others have been decent about it, and the tailor says tomorrow.
Someone lent me a shirt for the morning. I'll give it back as soon as I have my own.

blunt.li: I'm naked. Someone make me some pants.
Need clothes. Now.

cheerful.li: Naked as the day I was born! It's not so bad when the sun's out.
No clothes! I've been dodging people all day like it's a game.

gloomy.li: Naked. Hard to keep any dignity in a place like this.
Naked and cold and ashamed. Not a good day.

cold.li: No clothes. I know exactly who stared.
Without clothing. I've made it clear to the tailor that this is a priority.

plain.li: There's still a body lying out by the field. I went around it on the way to work.
Passed a corpse on the path this morning. The birds had found it first.
[summer] The body past the wall has started to smell. It needs burying.
[child] I saw a dead person lying in the grass. I didn't look at the face.
The body by the road is still there. Someone ought to do something.
Saw a dead raider by the path again today. The crows have been at it.
[summer] The smell from the body by the wall reached the kitchen today.

warm.li: That body is still by the gate. I laid a sack over the face before I went in.
I covered the dead stranger's face with my coat this morning. They deserved that much.
I said a few words over the body by the path before going on.

blunt.li: Bury the bodies. I'm sick of stepping around them.
Corpse still by the path. Bury it.
Who leaves bodies lying around?

cheerful.li: A body by the gate this morning. Ugh! I sang all the way to the field so I wouldn't think about it.
Walked past a dead body again. I've started taking the long way so it doesn't spoil my morning!
There's a corpse by the gate, but the sun's out and I'm alive, so I'm counting my blessings.

gloomy.li: Another body in the grass. One day it'll be one of us.
Passed the body again. I keep imagining it's someone I know.
The dead stay where they fall around here.

cold.li: Corpse near the path. Bad for morale, and it draws scavengers. It should have been hauled yesterday.
Unburied corpse. It's bad for morale and it draws scavengers.
A body by the gate, and it still hasn't been dealt with.

plain.li: Talked with {OTHER_nameDef} until the fire burned down. I didn't know half of what {OTHER_pronoun} told me.
{OTHER_nameDef} and I got talking about where we grew up. We have more in common than I thought.
{OTHER_nameDef} and I sat up talking about what we'd do if this place ever got safe.
Long talk with {OTHER_nameDef} about the people we left behind. I told {OTHER_objective} things I haven't told anyone here.
Found out today that {OTHER_nameDef} was afraid of the dark as a child, and still sleeps facing the door.
{OTHER_nameDef} asked me what I think happens after we die. I didn't have an answer, and {OTHER_nameDef} didn't either.
Washed up after supper with {OTHER_nameDef} and we talked the whole time. The water went cold before either of us noticed.
{OTHER_nameDef} told me about a sister {OTHER_pronoun} hasn't seen in years.
Talked with {OTHER_nameDef} about what we were before we came here. {OTHER_nameDef} doesn't miss it. I do.
Walked the wall with {OTHER_nameDef} after dark. We talked about our parents, mostly.

warm.li: I like {OTHER_nameDef} more every time we really talk. Tonight we really talked.
{OTHER_nameDef} told me something today that I don't think {OTHER_pronoun} has ever said out loud. I'll keep it safe.
Talked with {OTHER_nameDef} after supper. By the end I felt I'd known {OTHER_objective} for years.
{OTHER_nameDef} listened to me go on about home without once looking bored.

blunt.li: Good talk with {OTHER_nameDef}. Didn't expect that.
{OTHER_nameDef} talks sense. Spent the evening at it.
Long talk with {OTHER_nameDef}. Worth the lost sleep.
{OTHER_nameDef} asked hard questions tonight. I answered them.

cheerful.li: {OTHER_nameDef} told me the whole story of how {OTHER_pronoun} ended up here! I'd have listened all night.
Stayed up talking with {OTHER_nameDef}, and we planned a whole garden for when things calm down!
{OTHER_nameDef} and I found out we were born in the same month. We talked until supper went cold.
Had the best talk with {OTHER_nameDef}. I think we're friends now, properly.

gloomy.li: {OTHER_nameDef} told me about the people {OTHER_pronoun} lost, and I told {OTHER_objective} about mine. Neither of us slept much.
{OTHER_nameDef} said {OTHER_pronoun} doesn't expect to grow old here. I didn't argue.
Talked with {OTHER_nameDef} about whether any of this is worth it. We didn't decide.
{OTHER_nameDef} and I talked about home. Neither of us has one to go back to.

cold.li: Long conversation with {OTHER_nameDef}. I understand {OTHER_objective} better now, which is useful.
{OTHER_nameDef} talks freely once you let a silence go on long enough. I learned a lot tonight.
I let {OTHER_nameDef} do most of the talking. People tell you more that way.
{OTHER_nameDef} wanted someone to confide in. I listened, and I'll remember all of it.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} called me lazy today. I'd been up since before dawn.
Got told my work was sloppy by {OTHER_nameDef}, loud enough for the others to hear.
Still going over what {OTHER_nameDef} said this morning, and what I should have said back.
[child] {OTHER_nameDef} said I was a baby. I'm not.
{OTHER_nameDef} made a crack about my work with the others listening.
{OTHER_nameDef} said my cooking tasted like boot leather. I'll remember that at supper.

warm.li: Short words from {OTHER_nameDef} today. I'll assume {OTHER_pronoun} had a bad morning.
{OTHER_nameDef} said something cruel today. I hope {OTHER_pronoun} feels better tomorrow.
I'm not going to let {OTHER_nameDef} spoil my day. I'll try, anyway.

blunt.li: {OTHER_nameDef} has a mouth on {OTHER_objective}. Next time I'll answer it.
{OTHER_nameDef} insulted me. I won't forget it.
{OTHER_nameDef} had something to say. So will I, next time.

cheerful.li: Got an earful from {OTHER_nameDef} today, but I've already forgotten most of it!
{OTHER_nameDef} called me a fool. I'm choosing to take it as a joke!
An insult from {OTHER_nameDef} today. I've already forgiven it, mostly!

gloomy.li: Maybe {OTHER_nameDef} only said what the others think.
{OTHER_nameDef} said what I've been thinking about myself for weeks.
I'll be hearing what {OTHER_nameDef} said for days.

cold.li: After what {OTHER_nameDef} said today, I'll be less helpful to {OTHER_objective}.
{OTHER_nameDef} insulted me. I'll be civil with {OTHER_objective} and nothing more.
Noted {OTHER_nameDef}'s remark. It tells me what {OTHER_pronoun} really thinks.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} said I'd done good work on the wall. I've been thinking about it all evening.
Kind words from {OTHER_nameDef} today, out of nowhere.
On the path today, {OTHER_nameDef} stopped me to say thanks for the other day. I'd forgotten what I did.
[child] {OTHER_nameDef} said I was brave. I'm going to remember that.
{OTHER_nameDef} noticed I'd fixed the door and thanked me for it.
{OTHER_nameDef} told me I'm good at what I do. I wrote it down so I'd remember.
Passed {OTHER_nameDef} on the path and got a smile and a kind word.
{OTHER_nameDef} said it's good to have me here. I didn't know what to say.
[child] {OTHER_nameDef} said I'm a good helper. I helped all afternoon after that.

warm.li: At supper {OTHER_nameDef} said something kind to me, and it carried me through the evening.
{OTHER_nameDef} thanked me today. I'll find a way to thank {OTHER_objective} back.
Kind words from {OTHER_nameDef} at the end of a long day. That's what I'll remember about today.

blunt.li: Got a compliment from {OTHER_nameDef}. Didn't hate it.
{OTHER_nameDef} said I did good work. I did.
Nice of {OTHER_nameDef}. Noted.

cheerful.li: {OTHER_nameDef} told me I have a nice laugh! I've been laughing at everything since.
{OTHER_nameDef} said I brighten the place up! I'm going to try to live up to it.
A compliment from {OTHER_nameDef}! I've been grinning all evening.

gloomy.li: {OTHER_nameDef} was kind to me today. I didn't know what to say, so I just nodded.
{OTHER_nameDef} said something nice about my work. I didn't believe it, but I kept it.
{OTHER_nameDef} was kind to me today. It's been a while since anyone was.

cold.li: Praise from {OTHER_nameDef}. Either it's sincere or {OTHER_pronoun} wants something. I'll find out which.
{OTHER_nameDef} flattered me today. I'll keep {OTHER_objective} close.
Compliments from {OTHER_nameDef}. Good for my standing.

plain.li: Spent the night with {OTHER_nameDef}. Woke up with {OTHER_possessive} arm across my chest.
{OTHER_nameDef} and I went to bed early.
Lay awake talking with {OTHER_nameDef} long after we should have been asleep.
[winter] Cold night, warm bed. {OTHER_nameDef} steals the blankets.
{OTHER_nameDef} and I stayed in bed long after the others got up.
Fell asleep with my head on {OTHER_nameDef}'s shoulder.

warm.li: {OTHER_nameDef} fell asleep first, like always. I lay there listening to {OTHER_objective} breathe.
I woke before {OTHER_nameDef} and lay watching {OTHER_objective} sleep for a while.
{OTHER_nameDef} held my hand all night. I didn't want morning to come.

blunt.li: Slept well. {OTHER_nameDef} is the reason.
Good night with {OTHER_nameDef}.

cheerful.li: A lovely night with {OTHER_nameDef}! I've been humming all day.
{OTHER_nameDef}! That's all I'm writing today.
I've been smiling since breakfast, and {OTHER_nameDef} knows why!

gloomy.li: A good night with {OTHER_nameDef}. I'd like a lot more of them before this place gets us.
A good night with {OTHER_nameDef}. I keep thinking about how easily all of this could end.

cold.li: Night with {OTHER_nameDef}. Pleasant, and good for both our tempers.
{OTHER_nameDef} and I spent the night together. It settled us both.

plain.li: Told {OTHER_nameDef} how I feel. The answer was no.
Asked {OTHER_nameDef} to take a walk with me. {OTHER_nameDef} said {OTHER_pronoun}'d rather not.
Made a fool of myself with {OTHER_nameDef} today. I'll be keeping to the workshop for a while.
I asked {OTHER_nameDef} if we could spend more time together. {OTHER_nameDef} said no, kindly.
Turned down by {OTHER_nameDef} today. I'm trying not to replay it.

warm.li: {OTHER_nameDef} turned me down gently. We still sat together at supper.
{OTHER_nameDef} said no. I'm glad {OTHER_pronoun} was honest with me.

blunt.li: Asked {OTHER_nameDef}. Got turned down. Moving on.
{OTHER_nameDef} said no. Fine.

cheerful.li: {OTHER_nameDef} said no. Oh well! I'm still a catch.
{OTHER_nameDef} turned me down, but very politely! I'll survive.

gloomy.li: I knew {OTHER_nameDef} would turn me down, and I asked anyway.
{OTHER_nameDef} said no, and I keep hearing it.

cold.li: {OTHER_nameDef} declined. A miscalculation on my part, and I won't repeat it.
{OTHER_nameDef} is not interested. I'll stop wasting my time.

plain.li: Came to blows with {OTHER_nameDef} over whose turn it was to haul. My knuckles are still swollen.
{OTHER_nameDef} and I had it out behind the storeroom. Split lip, nothing worse.
[good] Traded punches with {OTHER_nameDef} today. I feel better than I have in weeks.
[child] {OTHER_nameDef} pushed me and I pushed back, and then we were rolling in the dirt.
Punched {OTHER_nameDef} today. Got punched back. We're both sorry, I think.
{OTHER_nameDef} shoved me, I shoved back, and someone had to pull us apart.
[good] Had it out with {OTHER_nameDef}. Bruised knuckles, clear head.

warm.li: Fought with {OTHER_nameDef}. I'm sorry for my part in it, and I'll tell {OTHER_objective} so tomorrow.
Fought with {OTHER_nameDef}. I'll bring {OTHER_objective} something warm to drink tomorrow and apologize.

blunt.li: {OTHER_nameDef} started it. I finished it.
Fought {OTHER_nameDef}. Won't be the last time.

cheerful.li: Had a scrap with {OTHER_nameDef}! We're both fine, and I think I won.
Got into a scrap with {OTHER_nameDef}! We shook hands afterward and had supper together.

gloomy.li: Another fight, this time with {OTHER_nameDef}. We're all wound too tight in here.
Fought with {OTHER_nameDef}. We're all on edge in here.

cold.li: Fought {OTHER_nameDef}. {OTHER_nameDef} bruises easily. Worth knowing.
Came to blows with {OTHER_nameDef}. I learned something about how {OTHER_pronoun} fights.

plain.li: I went down today, and {OTHER_nameDef} carried me in. I don't remember much of it.
Woke up in my bed with no idea how I got there. {OTHER_nameDef} carried me, they tell me.
Couldn't stand, so {OTHER_nameDef} dragged me back by the arms. My heels left two lines in the dirt.
[child] I got hurt and {OTHER_nameDef} carried me all the way home.
I don't remember much after I went down. {OTHER_nameDef} was there when I woke.
{OTHER_nameDef} carried me in while it was still dangerous out there. I owe {OTHER_objective} my life.

warm.li: When I went down, {OTHER_nameDef} got an arm under me and hauled me up. I held on to {OTHER_possessive} collar until we were inside.
I thanked {OTHER_nameDef} today. It didn't seem like enough.

blunt.li: {OTHER_nameDef} got me to safety. I owe {OTHER_objective} one.
{OTHER_nameDef} saved my life. I won't forget it.

cheerful.li: {OTHER_nameDef} carried me home like a sack of potatoes! I'm alive, so I'm not complaining.
Alive, thanks to {OTHER_nameDef}! I'm going to find a way to thank {OTHER_objective} properly.

gloomy.li: Carried in by {OTHER_nameDef} today. Next time there might be no one to do it.
{OTHER_nameDef} got me out. I keep thinking about what would have happened if {OTHER_pronoun} hadn't.

cold.li: {OTHER_nameDef} retrieved me when I was down. A useful person to keep alive.
{OTHER_nameDef} retrieved me at some risk. I'll repay it when the chance comes.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} taught me letters today. I can write my own name now.
Lessons with {OTHER_nameDef} at the desk. We did numbers until my head was full.
Learned from {OTHER_nameDef} which plants you can eat and which ones make you sick.
{OTHER_nameDef} showed me how to tie my boots so they don't come undone.
{OTHER_nameDef} taught me the names of the stars. I already forgot two.

warm.li: {OTHER_nameDef} is a good teacher and never gets cross when I get it wrong.
I like lessons with {OTHER_nameDef}. {OTHER_nameDef} never laughs when I get it wrong.

blunt.li: Had lessons. {OTHER_nameDef} talks a lot, but I learned stuff.
Lessons again. I learned stuff.

cheerful.li: {OTHER_nameDef} taught me to tie a proper knot! I've tied it on everything.
{OTHER_nameDef} taught me how to whistle, and I've been doing it all day!

gloomy.li: Lessons with {OTHER_nameDef} all morning. I tried hard and I still don't get it.
Lessons were hard today. {OTHER_nameDef} said I'll get it tomorrow.

cold.li: Sums with {OTHER_nameDef} today. I'll need them when I'm in charge of the stores.
{OTHER_nameDef} taught me sums. They're useful for knowing who has more.

plain.li: Gave {OTHER_nameDef} a reading lesson. We got through three whole pages.
Taught {OTHER_nameDef} to count to a hundred. We got stuck in the seventies.
Showed {OTHER_nameDef} how to hold a hammer without hitting a thumb.
{OTHER_nameDef} asked me why the sky is blue in the middle of the lesson. I made something up.
Taught {OTHER_nameDef} to plant seeds at the right depth. Half of them, anyway.

warm.li: {OTHER_nameDef} asked me questions all through the lesson. I answered the ones I could.
{OTHER_nameDef} remembered everything from last time. I was so proud.

blunt.li: Taught {OTHER_nameDef}. Kid's sharp.
Lesson with {OTHER_nameDef}. The kid listens. Good.

cheerful.li: Lesson with {OTHER_nameDef} today! {OTHER_nameDef} got every sum right by the end.
Taught {OTHER_nameDef} a song today, and now I can't get it out of my head!

gloomy.li: Letters with {OTHER_nameDef} today. I hope {OTHER_pronoun} grows up somewhere better than this.
{OTHER_nameDef} learns fast. I hope {OTHER_pronoun} gets the chance to use it.

cold.li: {OTHER_nameDef} is a slow learner. I'll try a different method tomorrow.
{OTHER_nameDef} is improving. Another pair of skilled hands in a few years.

plain.li: Sat down for a rest and {OTHER_nameDef} came and pushed {OTHER_possessive} head into my hand.
Got nuzzled by {OTHER_nameDef} on the way to the fields. Smelled of animal all day.
During my break, {OTHER_definite} wandered over and leaned against my legs until I gave {OTHER_objective} a scratch.
[child] I was sitting on the step and {OTHER_nameDef} came and pressed {OTHER_possessive} face right against mine. It tickled.
Sat down by the pen, and {OTHER_definite} leaned on me until I nearly fell over.
Spent my break scratching behind {OTHER_nameDef}'s ears.

warm.li: Bad morning, until {OTHER_nameDef} came over and nuzzled my hand.
At lunch {OTHER_nameDef} pushed {OTHER_possessive} nose into my hand, and I gave {OTHER_objective} the crust of my bread.
I sat with {OTHER_nameDef} after supper and told {OTHER_objective} about my day.

blunt.li: Nuzzled by {OTHER_nameDef} today. Good animal.
Got nuzzled. Good day.
Animals have more sense than people. Today was proof, thanks to {OTHER_nameDef}.

cheerful.li: Got a big nuzzle from {OTHER_nameDef} today! Best part of my day.
I think I'm {OTHER_nameDef}'s favorite now. I got nuzzled twice today!
Smelled like animal all day, and I don't care one bit!

gloomy.li: Only {OTHER_nameDef} seems pleased to see me lately.
At least {OTHER_nameDef} is happy to see me.
Today the only one glad to see me was {OTHER_nameDef}.

cold.li: I've been feeding {OTHER_nameDef} scraps, and today {OTHER_pronoun} nuzzled me. It's working.
The animal seeks me out. Feeding it was a sound decision.
Affection from {OTHER_nameDef}. Animals are simpler than people.

plain.li: The baby cried all through lunch, and most of the afternoon.
Crying from the next room again. I'd only just gotten to sleep.
Walked the baby up and down the hall until those little fists unclenched.
[child] The baby cried and cried. I put my pillow over my head.
The baby was teething and let all of us know about it.
Rocked the baby while the parents slept. It took most of an hour.
[child] The baby cried all through my story, so I stopped telling it.

warm.li: Sang to the baby until the little one fell asleep on my shoulder.
Took a turn walking the baby so the parents could get some sleep.
The baby wouldn't settle until I hummed. I hummed for a long time.

blunt.li: Baby screamed for hours. My ears are ringing.
Baby screamed all night. I'm exhausted.
Someone feed that baby.

cheerful.li: What lungs on that baby! That's a singer in the making.
The baby cried, so I made faces until the crying turned into giggling!
Tiny, but that baby has the loudest voice in the colony!

gloomy.li: Crying on and off all day. None of us will get any rest until the baby's older.
Crying again. I don't know how the parents stand it.
The baby cries, and I can't sleep, and then I can't work.

cold.li: Kept up by the crying. Babies are a cost the colony chose to take on.
The crying cost me a night's rest. I've noted it.
A baby's needs come first. I understand it. I don't enjoy it.

plain.li: Party tonight. Someone brought out the beer and we danced until the floor was sticky.
Went to the party for a bit. Ate too much and talked to people I usually don't.
Stayed at the party later than I meant to. My cheeks hurt from laughing.
[child] There was a party! I danced with everybody and ate two sweets.
Danced with someone I'd never spoken to before. We still haven't spoken.
Party tonight. I stayed near the food and was happy there.
[child] I stayed up past bedtime at the party, and the grown-ups forgot to send me to bed.

warm.li: Good party tonight. I'd forgotten some of these people could sing.
The party was lovely. I watched the newcomers loosen up and start laughing.
We were all there tonight, together, for once.

blunt.li: Party. Ate, drank, went to bed.
Party. Good beer. Bed.
Went. Danced once. Left.

cheerful.li: What a party! I danced until my feet gave out.
Danced until my feet hurt and then danced some more!
Best party yet! I'm still humming.

gloomy.li: There was a party. I stood by the wall with my drink and left early.
I went to the party and thought about the ones who aren't here anymore.
The others laughed a lot. I laughed a bit.

cold.li: Went to the party. Useful for seeing who talks to whom.
Attended the party. People talk freely after a few drinks.
A useful evening. I learned who dislikes whom.

plain.li: There was music tonight. I sat at the back with my eyes closed.
Went to the concert after supper. I didn't know any of the songs. The slow one was my favorite.
[!lowtech] Piano concert tonight. One key sticks, and the player found a way around it.
[child] I clapped all through the music. I want to learn to play when I'm bigger.
Music tonight. I tapped my foot so hard my shoe came off.
Somebody played a song from my home. I didn't know anyone else knew it.
[child] I sat at the front for the music and clapped in the wrong places.

warm.li: Music after supper, with my friends on either side of me. I didn't want it to end.
Music tonight. I watched the faces around me more than the player.
The concert put us all in a good mood. Supper was loud and happy.

blunt.li: Concert. Good music. Better than hauling.
Good music. Want more of it.
Concert. Liked it.

cheerful.li: A concert! I hummed the tune all the way to bed.
I sang along to every song I knew, and some I didn't!
What a night of music! My ears are still ringing.

gloomy.li: Sad songs at the concert. Those were the ones I liked.
The music was sad tonight. I liked it more than I can say.
The concert was beautiful. I went to bed lonelier than before.

cold.li: Attended the concert. Competent playing. Morale should hold for a few days.
The concert was well played. I noticed who didn't come.
Good music lifts the colony's mood. It was worth the hours.

plain.li: Heard our leader speak today. I stood at the back and ended up listening to every word.
The leader talked about what we're building here. I've been thinking about it while I work.
Good speech this morning. Short, too, which helps.
[child] There was a speech today. I didn't understand all of it, but I clapped at the end.
Our leader spoke after supper. I didn't agree with all of it, but I nodded along.
The speech was about pulling together. We'll see.
[child] There was a speech, and I stood on a crate so I could see.

warm.li: Our leader spoke about the ones we lost and the ones still here. I was glad I went.
A good speech. I looked around while it was going on, and we were all listening.
Our leader spoke about what we've built here. I felt proud.

blunt.li: Good speech. Back to work.
Speech was fine. A bit long.
Words are good. Work is better.

cheerful.li: Wonderful speech today! I want to go and build something big.
A rousing speech! I cheered louder than anyone.
I'm going to remember that speech for a long time!

gloomy.li: Inspiring speech. I'll feel it for a day or two, anyway.
A fine speech. I've heard fine speeches before.
Inspiring words. They'll have faded by the end of the week.

cold.li: A well-made speech. People will work harder this week.
The speech was effective. People are already working harder.
A competent speech. I took note of what was promised.

plain.li: Calm today. I'd forgotten what that felt like.
Slept twelve hours after the outburst. Woke up lighter.
Still embarrassed about the other day, but the knot in my chest is gone.
[child] I had a big tantrum yesterday. Today I feel good, and I said sorry.
Better today. Whatever was boiling over has gone quiet.
I said sorry to the people I shouted at. Most of them took it well.
[child] I was naughty yesterday. Today I was very good and helped carry wood.

warm.li: The others have been gentle with me since it happened. I feel like myself again.
I thanked the ones who put up with me last week. They brushed it off.
I feel steadier today. The others made room for me while I wasn't myself.

blunt.li: Lost it. Got it out. Feel better.
Head's clear. Back to work.
That's over. Good.

cheerful.li: Feeling much better today! I ate a huge breakfast.
I feel like I've had a bath on the inside. Wonderful!
Woke up light as a feather today!

gloomy.li: Better, since the breakdown. It'll build up again, but for now my head is clear.
Better now, for a while. It'll come back. It always does.
The weight's off for now. I don't trust it to stay off.

cold.li: The episode has passed. I'm functional, and I'd prefer it not be mentioned.
The episode is over. I've resumed full duties.
I've recovered. Some apologies were owed, and I made them.

plain.li: Early days here. The walls are half up and the fields are bare, but it feels like a start.
We've got some seed, some tools, and a plan. That's more than I've had in a while.
Woke up this morning and remembered where I was, and I didn't mind.
[child] We have a new home. I picked the spot for my bed.
Paced out where the walls will go. It took longer than it should have because I kept stopping to look at the view.
We ate our first meal here sitting on the supply crates.
Lots of work ahead. For once I don't mind.
Scratched my initials into the first post we put up.
[child] I found a frog by the water. I think it lives here too.

warm.li: Good people and a patch of land. I think we'll be all right here.
We're a small group, but a good one. I'm glad to be in it.
Shared out the first jobs today, and not one person complained.

blunt.li: New place. Lots to do. Let's get on with it.
Good start. Keep it going.
Ground's good. Water's close. We'll do.

cheerful.li: A whole new place to call ours! I walked all the way around it just to look.
It's ours! Every rock and weed of it.
Picked out the spot for a garden today, and a well, and a bench to sit on in the evenings!

gloomy.li: Hopeful days, for now. I've seen new starts go bad, but this one hasn't yet.
A fresh start. I've had a few of those. We'll see how this one goes.
Spirits are high. I'll enjoy it while it lasts.

cold.li: Morale is high, as it always is at the start. Now is the time to ask for hard work.
First days are when habits get set. I'm watching who works and who doesn't.
The site is defensible and the soil is decent. Our odds are reasonable.
